text:
The stock rose 0.18% today on the back of a sharp two-week rally—up 8.23% since late August—driven primarily by geopolitical tension in the Middle East and tight U.S. refining conditions. Iran's missile attacks on Kuwait this week pushed crude oil prices up more than 9% for the week, and U.S. refineries are currently running at 98% capacity with relatively lean inventory levels, a combination that typically improves profit margins for refiners like Marathon. The company has benefited from both the price floor created by rising crude costs and the operational squeeze that comes when refineries run hot and fuel supplies tighten.

The rally also reflects a broader shift in energy markets away from oversupply concerns—oil storage remains moderate at 711 million barrels—while geopolitical risk keeps buyers nervous. Gasoline and diesel inventories are also on the lower end of normal ranges, meaning any disruption to supply flows would strain the market further, which historically favors refiner margins.
